message.reasoning:
We need to produce a test class code that covers the test cases given, using JUnit5 and Mockito. The provided test class framework already includes some tests: DelegatesToGetMappedSchemaAndReturnsResult, NullArgument, EmptyString. However the test cases include many more scenarios: valid JSON schema string, valid YAML schema string, $ref external meta-schema, malformed JSON, malformed YAML, whitespace only, leading/trailing whitespace, empty JSON object, invalid $ref syntax, unresolvable external URI, unsupported spec version.

We need to adapt tests to use the factorySpy stub for getMappedSchema? But many cases require actual parsing and behavior (e.g., malformed JSON should throw JsonParseException). If we stub getMappedSchema to return mock, we bypass parsing. So we need separate tests where we use real factory (no stubbing) to actually parse. For valid cases we can just call getSchema and assert result is instance of JsonSchema.

We must not modify @Before/@After, but we can add additional test methods that use a real factory (maybe not spy). Could create a new factory instance inside test method.

We need to handle YAML detection; the factory uses getJsonMapper and getYamlMapper internally. So we can just call getSchema with YAML string and expect instance.

For exception cases: NullPointerException, IllegalArgumentException, JsonParseException, JsonSchemaException, IOException.

We need to import necessary classes: JsonSchema, JsonSchemaFactory, SpecVersion.VersionFlag, JsonSchemaException, JsonParseException (from com.fasterxml.jackson.core), etc.

We need to use parameterized tests where appropriate: group test cases: Valid Input - JSON Schema String (multiple cases) can be parameterized. Also Invalid Input - Null or Empty can be parameterized.

We must ensure that the spy stub does not interfere; we can use @BeforeEach to create spy for delegation test only; other tests can use fresh factory without stubbing. Could create separate test methods that instantiate a new factory (real) not spied.

Implementation plan:

- Keep existing fields factorySpy and mockSchema.

- Add parameterized test for valid inputs using MethodSource providing pairs of schema string and description. Use real factory: JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance(VersionFlag.V7). Call getSchema(schema) and assertNotNull and instance of JsonSchema.

- For YAML case, same.

- For $ref to external meta-schema: use schema with $ref to http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#. Expect instance, not exception.

- For edge cases: whitespace trimmed, empty JSON object.

- For malformed JSON: expect JsonParseException (or maybe JsonSchemaException). We'll catch the exception.

- For malformed YAML: expect JsonParseException.

- For invalid $ref syntax: expect JsonSchemaException.

- For unresolvable external URI: expect IOException (maybe wrapped). We'll call getSchema and catch.

- For unsupported spec version: expect IllegalArgumentException.

Note: The actual library may throw different exception types; we assume as per description.

We need to use assertThrows with appropriate class.

Potential need to mock static methods like JsonSchemaFactory.getInstance? Not needed.

We need to add imports for ParameterizedTest, MethodSource, etc.

We must not modify @BeforeEach; but we can still instantiate new factory inside test methods.

Potential conflict: The @BeforeEach currently sets up spy and stubs getMappedSchema for all tests; for tests that need real behavior, we can reset the stub to call real method using doCallRealMethod().when(factorySpy).getMappedSchema(...). But easier: create a new factory variable inside test method (not using factorySpy). So we can ignore factorySpy for those tests.

Thus we keep existing tests that rely on spy.

Add new test methods after existing ones.

Implement method source:

static Stream<Arguments> validSchemaProvider() { return Stream.of(Arguments.of("{\"type\":\"object\",\"properties\":{\"name\":{\"type\":\"string\"}}}", "Valid JSON schema"), Arguments.of("type: object\nproperties:\n  age:\n    type: integer", "Valid YAML schema"), Arguments.of("{\"$ref\":\"http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#\"}", "$ref meta-schema")); }

Edge cases provider.

Malformed provider.

Invalid $ref provider.

Unresolvable provider.

Unsupported spec version provider.

Now write code.

Make sure to import java.util.stream.Stream, org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.Arguments, org.junit.jupiter.params.provider.MethodSource, org.junit.jupiter.params.ParameterizedTest.

Also import com.networknt.schema.SpecVersion.VersionFlag.

Also include JsonSchemaException, JsonParseException, IOException.
